text:
incident-bot: Pager — Real-time latency regression detected for /v1/generate (region: us-west-2). p99 > 3s sustained for 5m, auto-alert triggered. Alert id: 43f7c. Paging SRE oncall: @alex.

alex: ACK. I'm looking now. Anyone on call for runtime? @nina?

nina: I'm on it, waking up dashboards. I see a p95 bump too, around 800ms -> 1.6s. p99 is spiking to ~3.5s.

maria: Noted — customer-facing streams reports coming in from CS. Paul, can you surface any enterprise hits?

paul: CS: two paying customers reporting slow streams and intermittent stalls. No 5xxs yet, mostly long tails and partial event chunks. Sending examples in DM.

alex: Quick litmus checks: 1) any recent canary/rollout? 2) autoscaler activity? 3) GPU pool saturation?

jonathan: Deployment history: we rolled out runtime v2.14-canary to 10% in us-west-2 ~8m ago. No rollbacks.

lena: Autoscaler logs show a burst of scale-ups but some pods stuck in Pending due to GPU allocation. Node pool reports 92% GPU usage.

nina: Tracing shows biggest tail at token streaming write path, large latencies on grpc_write for long sequences. Likely KV cache misses + long sequence generation hitting slower kernels.

alex: OK. Priority list: (A) quick mitigation to restore SLO, (B) investigate root cause and rollback plan, (C) customer comms.

maria: For (C) I'll draft a short CS note: "We're seeing elevated streaming latency in us-west-2; engineers are investigating. We'll update in 30 minutes."

alex: Mitigation options: 1) widen fallback routing to cheaper smaller model (rwd-small) for non-enterprise routes, 2) switch streaming to short-poll (disable SSE) for big responses, 3) increase cap on dedicated pool or add hot standby nodes, 4) route new traffic to us-east-1. Thoughts?

nina: Quickest is 1 + 3. We can change routing policy in the traffic-router API immediately. Command: 

```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/traffic-split \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"selector":"/v1/generate","fallback":"rwd-small","percent":30,"region":"us-west-2"}'
```

alex: I'll run that. Also asking infra to spin up 3 hot-gpu nodes (type: a10x) — Lena, can you escalate to cloud infra?

lena: Escalating now. Request ID: infra-req-7742. ETA 6-8m for node join.

jonathan: I'm watching canary. If the canary is related, we should roll it back from 10% to 0% while mitigation is live. Rollback command looks like: 

```
./deployctl rollback --service runtime --revision v2.14-canary --to stable
```

nina: Tracing also shows an increase in prefix cache misses for a subset of requests. If we can enable aggressive prefix caching for common prompts that would reduce tail latency. But that's a deploy change, not immediate.

alex: Ok execute quick steps now: 1) traffic-split -> rwd-small for 30% for /v1/generate 2) rollback canary to stable 3) set temporary throttles on background batch jobs that hit the same GPU pool. Nina/Jonathan, coordinate.

jonathan: Rolling back canary now. Running: `./deployctl rollback --service runtime --revision v2.14-canary --to stable` — started.

nina: Applying traffic-split now. Response: 200 OK. New split active.

alex: pausing background batches: `kubectl -n jobs scale deployment batch-workers --replicas=0` — doing it.

lena: infra status: 1 node provisioned, 2 still provisioning. PodPending backlog reduced from 12 -> 4.

paul: CS update: sent initial note to impacted customers. Asked for logs/IDs. Some customers are ok with temporary fallback if we mention possible quality change.

nina: Quick health checks after mitigations: p95 dropped to ~700ms, p99 down to ~1.8s within 90s. Streaming stall counts reduced by 60%.

alex: Nice. Keep the rollback + traffic-split in place while we root cause. We need full traces for the impacted requests — maria, can you collect example request IDs from CS?

maria: Got 4 session IDs from customers. Uploading to incident ticket now.

jonathan: Canary rollback finished, no failed pods. Confirming v2.14-canary is at 0%.

lena: Infra: new node joined, autoscaler stabilized. GPU utilization now ~72%.

nina: Captured a log excerpt showing long grpc write latency and kernel fallback lines: 

```
[stream] req=abc123 token_idx=192 grpc_write=1540ms kernel=fallback_quant32 kv_cache_miss=true
[serve] req=def456 token_idx=512 grpc_write=2480ms kernel=matmul_slow quant_fallback=true
```

alex: Looks like the runtime chose a slower kernel path for long sequences (quant fallback). Could be triggered by model variant or memory pressure. Follow-ups: (1) dig into kernel selector telemetry, (2) validate quant profiles for that model variant, (3) run a targeted load test reproducing long-sequence streaming. Nina/Jonathan will own.

maria: CS: customers want ETA for full resolution. I suggested 2 hours for a root-cause update given kernel/quant investigation.

paul: Also requested: list of impacted customer orgs + mitigation applied (fallback to rwd-small).

alex: I'll create a short incident note in status page: include impact, mitigation, next steps.

incident-bot: Alert update: severity -> elevated (SLO-breach), page continues.

nina: Quick reproduction plan: run a batch of long-sequence streaming requests against canary vs stable with quant profiles. If stable performs better, it's likely canary introduced kernel selector change. If not, infra pressure is likely.

jonathan: I'll run the reproduction in isolated cluster and attach profiler traces. ETA 45m.

lena: Node provisioning completed. No further pod Pending. Autoscaler logs look normal now.

alex: Good. For now leave traffic-split in place and keep CS note updated every 30m. If p99 stays <2s for 15m, we can start a cautious rollback of the traffic-split (reduce fallback percent).

maria: Made a note — next customer update scheduled in 25m.

incident-bot: New event: p99 dipped below 2s for 10m. Continue monitoring.

nina: Reproduction started. Attaching profiler link: https://perf.internal/profiles/incident-1718249999 (internal).

jonathan: Got the first reproduction run: stable median 600ms p99 1.1s, canary median 650ms p99 3.2s. So canary looks suspicious.

alex: Great find. We can keep mitigations and prepare a permanent rollback of canary. Also plan a postmortem focused on kernel selector/quantization interaction.

paul: CS: customers replied thank you, some requested a brief changelog note when resolved.

maria: Update posted to status page: short description + current mitigations + timeframe.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated. SLOs returning to baseline. Incident owner: alex.

alex: Closing loop: Nina/Jonathan will produce RCA draft within 48h, include root cause, why kernel fallback happened, and remediation (fix selector, guardrails for canary rollout). Maria/Paul will finalize customer comms. I'll file follow-up tasks.

lena: One more infra note: increase node pool buffer by 10% for this cluster to reduce PodPending during spikes. Filing infra ticket.

maria: Final CS note queued.

incident-bot: Incident closed: all alerts resolved for 30m, reverting page to passive. Incident link: https://incidents.internal/1718249999

alex: Thanks everyone — good coordinated response.

maria: Good job team. :thumbsup:

nina: I'll start the RCA draft.

jonathan: Adding reproduction artifacts to ticket.

paul: Closing customer loop after RCA.

lena: Will follow up on infra ticket.
